subject: Post-call: CuraLogic security starter — prefill decision & evidence asks
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Emma Holt <emma.holt@curalogic.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Oct 2026 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap + next steps: security starter and questionnaire preference

Hi Emma — thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap and a few clarifying questions so we can start the right questionnaire path.

Recap (from our call)
- Primary ask: CuraLogic needs a vendor security package that satisfies HIPAA-covered processing and internal cloud controls review.
- You said: preferred approach is to collect evidence for PHI handling (BAA required) and have a controls questionnaire for cloud controls.
- Timeline: rough procurement decision window ~4–6 weeks.

Clarifying questions (so we route correctly):
1) Data scope: can you confirm the types of PHI you expect us to process (e.g., patient identifiers, claims data, device telemetry)? This determines the evidence set.
2) Residency: do you require EU residency for any datasets, or is US-only acceptable for the initial deployment?
3) BAA: will your legal team require Redwood to sign a standalone BAA or is it acceptable to include BAA language in the master services agreement?
4) Questionnaire preference: you mentioned SIG-lite on the call — do you want the full SIG (Consensus) or CAIQ (cloud-focused) as the starting form? We can prefill one and provide the supporting evidence bundle.
5) Encryption/key mgmt: are your reviewers looking for customer-managed keys (BYOK) in addition to our standard envelope encryption?

Proposed next steps
- We can prefill a CAIQ focused on cloud controls and attach SOC2 evidence for the PHI processing controls in parallel (this tends to speed reviewer work). If you explicitly want the Consensus SIG, we’ll route to that instead — both are fine but have slightly different evidence maps.
- Stephanie will assemble a short evidence bundle (SOC2 summary, encryption notes, network diagrams) and a CAIQ prefill draft for you to review.
- Schedule a 30-min tech deep-dive this week to walk engineers through data flow and answer any control-specific questions.

I’ve attached a prefill draft template and our SOC2 summary for reference. Please reply with: 1) questionnaire preference (SIG vs CAIQ), 2) confirmation on PHI types + residency, and 3) 2–3 names from procurement/security to include on follow-ups.

Thanks — talk soon.

—
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0126
redwood.com

Attachments:
- redwood-qa-prefill-draft.xlsx (Spreadsheet: CAIQ prefill starter)
- redwood-soc2-summary.pdf (PDF: high-level SOC2 controls summary)

From: Emma Holt <emma.holt@curalogic.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + next steps: security starter and questionnaire preference

Thanks Stephanie — helpful recap. Quick answers below.

1) PHI scope: patient identifiers (name, DOB, MRN), clinical notes (text), and device telemetry associated with patient IDs. No claims adjudication data for phase 1.
2) Residency: US residency required for initial pilot; we may request EU residency later for EU clients but not for pilot.
3) BAA: we need a standalone BAA to be in place before production onboarding. Legal will need to review standard language.
4) Questionnaire preference: our security team prefers Consensus SIG (full) so they can map to their risk framework. If you can provide a prefilled SIG and a CAIQ as a supplemental shorter view, that would be ideal.
5) Encryption: our security reviewers will expect the option for customer-managed keys (BYOK) for production, but for pilot your standard managed keys are acceptable. Please document the BYOK path.

Can you also confirm whether Redwood can provide token-level redaction options and a sample data retention policy for the types above? That will speed legal review.

Availability for a 30-min tech session: Tue 19 Oct 2026 11:00–12:00 PT or Wed 20 Oct 09:00–10:30 PT.

Regards,
Emma Holt
Head of Security Operations | CuraLogic
emma.holt@curalogic.com
security@curalogic.com

Emma — perfect, thanks for the fast answers. Short replies inline and next actions: 

- PHI scope: noted (patient identifiers, clinical notes, device telemetry). We will map controls and retention to those classes.
- Residency: US-only for pilot — we’ll mark that in the evidence set.
- BAA: we can provide our standard BAA; I’ll loop Legal if you want to start with draft language now.
- Preference: we’ll prefill the full Consensus SIG as primary and also produce a CAIQ extract for cloud reviewers. That dual-output approach works well.
- Encryption/BYOK: Redwood supports envelope encryption with customer-managed keys for production; I’ll attach a short BYOK implementation note and a sample config doc.

Regarding token-level redaction and retention: we offer configurable redaction at ingest and token-level masking options — I’ll include the product note and a sample retention policy we use with other HIPAA customers.

Next actions (we’ll own these this week):
1) Stephanie to upload a SIG prefill draft (attached as the CAIQ prefill for now — our SIG prefill is in progress) + evidence bundle (SOC2 summary, network diagram, BYOK note).
2) Ben (cc) will coordinate with our Legal on a draft BAA to share with your counsel if you want to expedite.
3) Schedule 30-min tech call: Tue 19 Oct 2026 11:00 PT works for us — I’ll send a calendar invite shortly.

Can you confirm stakeholders for evidence shares (names + emails)? Emma, you mentioned procurement and a security reviewer — names will help speed up sharing.

Thanks — attaching the current CAIQ/controls prefill we mentioned.

—
Stephanie
